context: Data visualization — small-multiples network graph showing network evolution over 6 months, with force-directed layouts per panel and edge-change encoding (new/removed/persistent edges)
first_impression: Clean, well-structured layout with a sensible Tol palette, but the panels feel uniform and the force layouts produce scattered, hard-to-compare graphs across months.
what_works: The Tol color palette (green/pink/gray for new/removed/persistent edges) is a deliberate, accessible choice that avoids the schemeCategory10 default. Panel headers with monospace node/edge counts in the corner is a nice typographic detail.
what_doesnt: Because each panel runs an independent force simulation, the node positions are not spatially consistent across months — making it impossible to visually track individual nodes evolving over time, which undermines the core comparative purpose. The legend and controls bar feels cramped, mixing two buttons and a legend on one line without clear separation.
